text:
Testing is a crucial part of software development. It generally falls into two main categories. Unit tests check small, individual pieces of code, like a single function, to ensure they work correctly in isolation. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different parts of the system work together properly, catching problems that only appear when modules interact.

Many developers also practice test-driven development, or TDD. In this approach, you write a failing test before writing the actual code. This forces you to think carefully about what the code should do. The greatest benefit of testing is the confidence it provides. When you can run a full suite of tests quickly, you feel safe making changes and improving your code, knowing that any mistakes will be caught immediately.
